# self-update: brew: one broken upstream cask aborts the whole run

Let `self-update all` survive a cask that cannot be downloaded for reasons outside the dotfiles. **Motivation:** the casks come from upstream taps that are bumped by bots, and from time to time a bump points at a file that does not exist: a typo in the version, or a vendor that pulls a build after the bump. Then `brew bundle` exits non-zero, `set -e` stops the script, and everything after it is skipped (the rest of the brew steps, Docker images, Go tools, Oh My Zsh) although none of it depends on that cask. The installed app keeps working, and the upstream fix usually lands within hours, so the only thing the failure gives is a lost update run.

```
$ self-update all
...
==> Fetching downloads for: chatgpt
✘ Cask chatgpt (26.1002.51308)
Error: Download failed on Cask 'chatgpt' with message: Download failed: https://persistent.oaistatic.com/codex-app-prod/ChatGPT-darwin-arm64-26.1002.51308.zip
curl: (56) The requested URL returned error: 404
Upgrading chatgpt has failed!
`brew bundle` failed! 1 Brewfile dependency failed to install
```

Expected: on request, a run goes past a failed package download, finishes the other steps, then lists what failed and exits non-zero, so the failure stays visible to the user and to scripts. The default stays strict: a run without the request stops at the first error, as today.

Out of scope: failures that point at the dotfiles themselves (`brew update`, `git pull`, `go generate`), which keep stopping the run; fixing the upstream casks, which is done in their taps.
